hypotheses.construction_plan: The two branches of the Piecewise expression are evaluations of a single binary kernel K. The branch K(n,m) is the kernel at the off-diagonal argument pair (n,m); the branch K(n,n) is the kernel at the diagonal argument pair (n,n). The piecewise guard Ne(n,m) selects the off-diagonal evaluation when n and m differ, and the diagonal evaluation otherwise. Both are generated by specializing the same latent kernel K(a,b) to concrete argument pairs.
required_assumptions: n and m are well-formed terms in the domain of K
the substitution a:=n, b:=m and a:=n, b:=n are valid in the ambient language
proof_obligations: K(n, m) - specialize[K(a, b), a=n, b=m] = 0
K(n, n) - specialize[K(a, b), a=n, b=n] = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The two subexpressions are non-identical but both use the same function symbol K with related argument lists. No extra structure is required beyond treating K as a shared binary function and specializing its arguments; the piecewise wrapper merely decides which specialization to use based on the equality of n and m.
